title: A cofinal system of finite-presentation models with eventual flatness
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a finitely presented flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $I$ be the set of finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras $R_i\subseteq R$, ordered by inclusion [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Then there exist $i\in I$, a finitely presented $R_i$-algebra $B_i$, an $R$-algebra isomorphism $\theta:B_i\otimes_{R_i}R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$, and $j_f\geq i$ with the following properties. For $j\geq i$ put $B_j=B_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j$, with the tensor-induced transition homomorphisms [def-weil-module-base-change] [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. The tails $I_{\geq i}$ and $I_{\geq j_f}$ are small nonempty directed sets and the inclusions identify each ring colimit $\varinjlim R_j$ with $R$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Every $R_j\to B_j$ for $j\geq i$ is finitely presented, and every such map for $j\geq j_f$ is flat. For every $j\geq i$ there is a compatible $R$-algebra isomorphism $\theta_j:B_j\otimes_{R_j}R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$. The squares $R_j\to B_j$, $R_j\to R$, $B_j\to S$, $R\to S$ are cocartesian, meaning that maps from $S$ to a commutative ring are uniquely equivalent to pairs of maps from $B_j$ and $R$ agreeing on $R_j$. For $i\leq j\leq k$, the natural map $B_j\otimes_{R_j}R_k\to B_k$ is an isomorphism compatible with $\theta_j$ and $\theta_k$.

source.place: Tag 05FE, lemma-Noetherian-approximation-flat, proof via lemma-Noetherian-approximation-flat-module: the flat algebra-model construction, expanded to its cofinal subalgebra system and compatible cocartesian squares.

proof.text: For any $a\in I$, the tail $J_a=\{j:R_a\subseteq R_j\}$ is a set of subsets of $R$, hence small, and contains $a$. Two members generated by finite sets $E,F$ are bounded by the subring generated by $E\cup F$, which still contains $R_a$. Every $r\in R$ lies in the subring generated by $R_a$ and $r$. Given compatible ring maps $h_j:R_j\to T$, define $h(r)=h_j(r)$ using any $j$ containing $r$. A common upper bound makes this independent of $j$ and proves preservation of addition, multiplication and $1$; it also proves uniqueness. Thus $R$ is the ring colimit of every tail. The identical argument, using the image of $\mathbf Z$ as the least subring, applies to $I$ itself.

source.place: Tag 05N9, lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras (1): the directed base system; direct verification of its colimit

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-fp-algebra-descent] to this small filtered diagram with colimit $R$ and the finitely presented $R$-algebra $S$. Obtain $i$, a finitely presented $R_i$-algebra $B_i$, and, reversing the supplied isomorphism if necessary, $\theta:B_i\otimes_{R_i}R\simeq S$. For $j\geq i$ define $B_j=B_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j$ and the transition by $b\otimes r\mapsto b\otimes r$ with $r$ viewed in the larger subring. At $j=i$ use the canonical identification $B_i\otimes_{R_i}R_i\simeq B_i$.

By the tensor pushout universal property, for $i\leq j\leq k$ the formulas $(b\otimes r)\otimes t\mapsto b\otimes rt$ and $b\otimes t\mapsto(b\otimes1)\otimes t$ give inverse $R_k$-algebra homomorphisms $B_j\otimes_{R_j}R_k\simeq B_k$. The tensor balancing relation verifies both composites. The same formulas with $R$ in place of $R_k$, followed by $\theta$, define $\theta_j$; explicitly $\theta_j((b\otimes r)\otimes t)=\theta(b\otimes rt)$. These formulas agree for every transition, and identities and compositions agree on pure tensors, hence everywhere. Finally a pair $u:B_j\to T$, $v:R\to T$ agreeing on $R_j$ induces the unique map $(b_j\otimes t)\mapsto u(b_j)v(t)$; composing with $\theta_j^{-1}$ proves exactly the asserted cocartesian square, also for ring maps to an arbitrary commutative ring $T$.

source.place: Tensor pushout calculation for the base-change squares in Tag 05N9 (1)

proof.text: Finite presentation is preserved by base change: apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] (1) to $R_i\to B_i$ and $R_i\to R_j$. Its tensor order $R_j\otimes_{R_i}B_i$ is identified with $B_j$ by exchanging the factors, $r\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes r$, with the same formula as inverse. Thus all $R_j\to B_j$ are finitely presented.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-flat-ring-map] with index set $J_i$, distinguished index $i$, base rings $A_j=R_j$, $A=R$, and distinguished algebras $B_0=R_i$, $C_0=B_i$, $\varphi_0:R_i\to B_i$. The base colimit is step 1 and $\varphi_0$ is finitely presented by step 2. The limit map identifies with $R\to S$ by $\theta$ and the factor exchange from step 3, so is flat by hypothesis. The conclusion supplies $j_f\geq i$ for which all $R_j\to B_j$ with $j\geq j_f$ are flat. Step 1 applies also to $J_{j_f}$, supplying the remaining tail and colimit assertions.
